metadata.doc_note: ZITADEL custom-login SAML finalization endpoint binds a created session to a SAML request; docs do not expose a direct ACS endpoint that accepts arbitrary SAMLResponse for broker login testing.

saml.description: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows.
saml.note: IdP-initiated attempts failing are by design and should not be flagged as flow-coherence bugs.

saml.description: The SAML SSO endpoint returns HTTP 200 even when the SAML response contains an error status.
saml.note: Tests must inspect SAML StatusCode/message rather than relying on HTTP status alone.

saml.description: When requested_token_type is id_token in token exchange, the returned ID token is placed in the access_token field and token_type is N_A.
saml.note: This looks odd but follows the documented RFC 8693 behavior in ZITADEL; do not treat it as token confusion by itself.

saml.description: Token introspection reports active only when the requesting client is part of the token audience.
saml.note: An inactive result can be due to audience mismatch of the introspecting client, not token invalidity.

saml.description: The SAML SSO endpoint returns HTTP 200 even when the SAML response contains an error status.
saml.note: Use SAML StatusCode/content, not HTTP status alone, to determine success or failure.

saml.description: ZITADEL issues opaque access tokens by default rather than JWTs.
saml.note: Do not flag inability to locally decode access tokens as a platform defect.

saml.constraint: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow. Do NOT test IdP-initiated SAML logins against ZITADEL; a valid SAML test must begin with the SP sending a SAMLRequest to /saml/v2/SSO and then evaluate the resulting SAMLResponse handling.

For SAML security tests against ZITADEL as SAML IdP, /saml/v2/SSO returns HTTP 200 even on protocol errors; the actual success or failure is encoded in the SAML StatusCode/message, not the HTTP status. The fuzzer MUST parse the SAML response body and MUST NOT treat HTTP 200 as authentication success by itself.

For SAML brokering tests where ZITADEL is the broker and downstream flow is OIDC, the sequence MUST include the OIDC authorization and token exchange steps. A SAML upstream success does not itself yield the bearer token used for verification APIs; use /oauth/v2/authorize then /oauth/v2/token and use access_token as session_token.

When testing I5 scope/audience binding on ZITADEL, remember that reserved scopes can add audience or enforce organization membership. In particular, urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud adds that project to the access-token audience, and urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforces membership in the selected organization. Do NOT treat audience expansion caused by requested reserved scopes as a broker overgrant bug.

For multi-organization SAML/OIDC tests, if organization-specific settings override defaults, the auth request MUST include the organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}; otherwise ZITADEL uses default settings and may select a different IdP/login policy than intended, causing false I3/I4/I5 results.

For token introspection and userinfo verification, the requesting client must be part of the token audience. Introspection returns active=true only if the requesting client is part of the token audience. The fuzzer MUST ensure the application/client used for introspection or downstream API checks is included in aud, or failures will be false negatives rather than authorization-binding bugs.

Token exchange audience on ZITADEL can only be reduced, not expanded: requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and cross-org tests, a rejection is by design if the requested audience was not already present upstream.

Token exchange scope on ZITADEL may differ from the requested scope because ZITADEL validates the input and always returns the final scope in the response. For I5 scope-escalation tests, compare the returned scope and claims to the upstream authorization, not merely the requested scope string.

The token exchange resource parameter is currently not supported by ZITADEL and supplying it results in invalid_target. Do NOT use resource-based token exchange tests as evidence of authorization bugs on this platform.

For token exchange tests requesting requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token, ZITADEL returns the ID token in the access_token field and sets token_type=N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT use that returned access_token as a bearer session token for verify_granted_identity or other API calls.

For I2 freshness tests involving JWT-based client authentication or JWT profile grants, ZITADEL requires iat to be no older than 1 hour and aud to include the ZITADEL issuing domain. Use template times such as iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} for control tokens; otherwise LOGIN_FAILED may reflect malformed client assertions rather than the freshness property under test.

ZITADEL does not support the OAuth 2.0 SAML 2.0 Profile grant. Do NOT attempt to test SAML bearer grant behavior at /oauth/v2/token as part of the SAML profile; SAML-relevant flows are browser SSO and SAML identity brokering, not RFC 7522 token grant processing.

When using private_key_jwt or JWT profile with /oauth/v2/token or /oauth/v2/introspect, the JWT header MUST include kid matching the downloaded key ID. Missing or wrong kid causes key identification failure and invalid_client/invalid_grant outcomes unrelated to the invariant under test.

ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows. Do NOT test IdP-initiated SAML login against ZITADEL as the SAML IdP; a valid SAML test must begin with the SP sending a SAMLRequest to /saml/v2/SSO and evaluate the returned SAMLResponse.

The SAML /saml/v2/SSO endpoint returns HTTP 200 even on authentication/protocol errors; failure is conveyed inside the SAML StatusCode and message. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat HTTP 200 alone as successful SAML authentication for I1/I2/I5 tests.

For SAML brokering into ZITADEL as SP, Login V2/programmatic flows use the provider-specific ACS Intent API URL shown in provider details, while Login V1/standard browser flows use the ACS Login Form URL. The fuzzer MUST use the correct ACS URL for the flow under test or results are invalid.

When testing SAML external IdPs in ZITADEL Login V2, user creation fails unless required user fields are mapped from IdP attributes via an Actions V2 response manipulation on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent. A failed first-login without this mapping is setup failure, not a security rejection.

SAML provider setup in ZITADEL is metadata-driven. Trust anchors, endpoints, and issuer details are imported from metadata URL/XML. For I1 trust tests, the fuzzer MUST distinguish between metadata-derived defaults and explicitly overridden settings; changing only the runtime assertion without changing imported metadata may correctly fail by design.

For SAML issuer/audience tests against ZITADEL as SP, the SP Entity ID/Audience expected by upstream IdPs is the ZITADEL Metadata URL, and the ACS endpoint is the ZITADEL ACS URL. Assertions with a different Audience should be rejected; however, misconfiguring the upstream IdP with the wrong ZITADEL metadata/ACS values invalidates the test setup.

External IdP availability is gated by login policy. The fuzzer MUST enable 'External Login allowed' in login settings before attempting SAML broker logins; otherwise login failure is by-design policy enforcement, not an authentication bug.

If organization-specific login settings override default settings, the authorization request MUST include the organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} to select the intended org context. Without this scope, ZITADEL may use default instance settings and a SAML provider may appear missing or different by design.

Token exchange audience narrowing is enforced: requested audience must be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and cross-org tests, the fuzzer MUST first obtain control tokens whose audience already contains the target project/app; otherwise rejection is expected and not evidence of a bug.

Token exchange scope behavior is not monotonic narrowing. ZITADEL documentation states scope can be entirely different from supplied tokens and can extend or decrease the new token, subject to validation. For I5 scope-escalation tests, compare granted claims/scope against upstream authorization and audience, not against an assumption that requested scope must always be a subset.

The token exchange parameter resource is currently unsupported and always results in invalid_target. The fuzzer MUST NOT use resource to test audience binding on ZITADEL; use the audience parameter instead.

When requested_token_type is urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token, ZITADEL returns the ID token in the access_token field and sets token_type to N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT use that returned access_token as a Bearer credential for verify_granted_identity or resource access; obtain a real access token or request openid with an access-token type.

ZITADEL introspection returns active=true only if the token is active and the requesting client is part of the token audience. For verification, the fuzzer MUST introspect with a client that belongs to the token audience; otherwise active=false is by design and not token invalidity.

ZITADEL access tokens are opaque by default. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume local JWT validation semantics for all access tokens; use /oauth/v2/introspect or explicitly request JWT token type where needed.

For private_key_jwt client authentication on token or introspection endpoints, the client assertion iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour, aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain, and the JWT header MUST carry kid matching the registered keyId. Failures under these conditions are setup errors, not security findings.

For I2 freshness control tests using JWT profile or private_key_jwt, use time claims relative to now: iat={{now_epoch}}, exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} for valid controls. Assertions older than 1 hour are rejected by design for client-auth JWTs.
ZITADEL rejects expired ID tokens used as subject_token in token exchange. For I2 tests involving token exchange with ID tokens, an expired subject ID token failing exchange is by design.

ZITADEL does not support Resource Owner Password Credentials. Do NOT expect or extract login_with_password for SAML profiles; admin/setup authentication must use another documented method such as client credentials, PAT, or interactive browser login.

saml.constraint: For SAML broker tests against ZITADEL, the user-facing login is still OIDC. A valid sequence MUST use /oauth/v2/authorize followed by the brokered SAML step and then /oauth/v2/token to obtain the Bearer access token used for verification calls. Do NOT treat SAML as returning an API bearer token directly.

ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow. The fuzzer MUST initiate the flow first and preserve request state (including the SAML request ID / InResponseTo relationship). IdP-initiated SAML tests are invalid against this platform and will produce false positives.
saml.source: guides/integrate/login/saml.mdx: ZITADEL supports only the SP-initiated flow; login-ui/saml-standard.mdx

saml.constraint: The documented SAML SSO endpoint /saml/v2/SSO always returns HTTP 200 even on SAML protocol errors; failure is conveyed inside the SAML StatusCode/message. For SAML protocol tests, do NOT interpret HTTP 200 as successful authentication.

For custom-login SAML flows, finalizing a SAML request requires an authorization header from an account permitted with the IAM_LOGIN_CLIENT role, plus the latest session token from session creation/update. Tests that omit this role or use stale session tokens will fail due to setup, not due to SAML security behavior.

When testing SAML identity brokering in Login V2, user creation will fail unless required user fields are mapped from IdP attributes via Actions V2 on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent. A failed first-login without this mapping is a setup failure, not an authentication-security result.

External IdP login must be enabled in the login policy (External Login allowed), either at instance default settings or organization settings. If not enabled, SAML broker login tests will fail before reaching provider validation.

If organization-specific login settings override defaults, the authorization request MUST include the reserved organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}; otherwise ZITADEL may show default IdPs/settings and route the test to the wrong provider configuration.

For I2 freshness tests on exchanged or brokered tokens, include a control flow with a valid token and compare against the attack token. ZITADEL returns HTTP 401 on invalid/expired userinfo tokens and invalid_grant/invalid_request style OAuth errors on token endpoint failures; without a control, failures are ambiguous.
Token exchange resource parameter is not supported and always results in invalid_target. Do NOT use resource-based token exchange tests against ZITADEL.

When requested_token_type=id_token in token exchange, ZITADEL returns the ID token in the access_token field and sets token_type=N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT use that returned access_token as a Bearer token for verify_granted_identity or resource access.

ZITADEL token exchange can legitimately extend or decrease scope relative to the supplied token, subject to validation. For I5 scope-escalation tests, compare the resulting scope/claims against documented validation behavior and original authorization context; do not assume token exchange is always scope-preserving.

Introspection returns active=true only if the token is active AND the requesting client is part of the token audience. For verification and audience-binding tests, a false/limited introspection result from the wrong client is by design, not evidence of token invalidity.

ZITADEL uses opaque access tokens by default. The fuzzer MUST use the returned access_token as the Bearer credential and SHOULD rely on /oidc/v1/userinfo or /oauth/v2/introspect for verification rather than assuming local JWT parsing is always possible.

For private_key_jwt authentication to token or introspection endpoints, the client assertion iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour, aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain, and the JWT header MUST include kid. Failures here are client-auth setup errors, not token-validation bugs.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Zitadel management API paths are relative to /management/v1/ (org-scoped). Use the correct REST gateway paths, NOT gRPC Connect paths. Proto RPC names like 'zitadel.idp.v2.IdentityProviderService/...' do NOT work as HTTP paths.
